newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end sharply down as financials slide.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end sharply down as financials slide.

text.p: Taiwan share prices finished sharply lower on Friday as financials took a tumble on the government's plan to sell down holdings in the island's "big three" state-run banks, brokers said.
The weighted index, falling below a recent 6,800-support level, finished 110.48 points or 1.61 percent lower at 6,765.93. Turnover was T$69.69 billion, somewhat muted from recent days.
Financial shares were hit hardest, falling 2.66 percent.
The finance ministry said on Friday it may sell down holdings in the island's "big three" state-run banks to alleviate the state budget deficit.
The selldown plan fuelled fears that the state, widely seen to have started November's bold bull run, now may be considering actions to cool the over-heated stock market, brokers said.

"The psychological impact of the news is greater than the actual impact. There are fears that the government is turning cautious towards the market's sharp rises," said Joe Chiou, an analyst of Taiwan Securities Investment.

"Since the market's recent rally was fuelled by the government's supportive policies, people are especially worried about the timing of this (selldown) plan," Lin Long-hsien, an analyst of United Securities.
Share prices of the "big three" state banks were down. Chang Hwa fell T$1 or 0.65 percent to T$154, First Commercial T$3 or 1.81 percent to T$163 and Hua Nan T$3 or 2.35 percent to T$124.5.
Despite the market tumble, newly listed banking share UWCCB surged the daily seven percent limit to T$62 in its debut.
Brokers saw little impact of South Africa's announced plan to switch diplomatic ties to Beijing from Taipei in 1997.
"Except for the fact that it is a major political setback, investors don't think it will have a devastating impact on the market," United's Lin said.
